## SECTION C: READING COMPREHENSION (10 marks)

Read the following passage and answer the questions below it in complete sentences. Use your own words as far as you can.

> My name is Joan. My story begins from when I was a little girl, an innocent child at the hands of a cruel grandfather. About twice a year, my family would fly out to where my grandparents lived. That's how my young life started, being violently raped and abused over and over again. And that's how the sexual abuse continued throughout my entire childhood.
>
> When I reached 9th grade, I was sent away to an all-girls boarding school. I had been in and out of schools every year of high school and when I was in 11th grade (in yet again, a new school) that's where I met Perpetua. She was my teacher, and I confided in her, the secret that I had been holding in all those years. She responded with kindness and compassion. But soon after, she went on to take advantage of my vulnerability, and continued the horrid pattern that my life had claimed. She would crawl into my bed at night and exploit and shatter whatever human part of me my grandfather had left behind. She stole any innocence that had been forgotten, she tore me apart once again-leaving me more broken than I had ever been.
>
> The next two years went by, filled with numbness and unbearable pain. Filled with emotions I had ever known existed. Filled with an emptiness that was so hollow, I was a walking dead person. The endless amount of sleepless nights became a ritual in my twisted schedule. The daily confusion and absolute loss that consumed me is indescribable. This torturous hell was my life as I had come to know it.
>
> Then I found Pandora's. I found a place that not only accepted me for who I was, but supported me for what I went through. A place where not only was I understood, but I in turn learned to understand more and more about the devastating effects of sexual abuse. I learned that it was normal to have flashbacks, to have body memories. I learned a whole new language and turned to this new world where things finally made sense. I spent countless hours glued to my computer screen filled with excitement and relief.
>
> Pandora's has opened my mind and touched my soul. The amount of strength and courage shown by each and every member of this wonderful community, has taught me life lessons that I will take with me wherever I go. Pandora's has opened my mind and touched my soul. It has given me the ability to reach out to others in my situation and the strength that I need to go on every day. It has given me a sense of stability that I don't think I would have been able to find anywhere else. A place to go wherever and whenever I need. Pandora's has been a huge tool that I've used to move forward with. It continues to give me hope – a new sense of hope each and every day.
>
> I am still continuing on in my healing journey. There aren't enough words to express my gratitude and appreciation to those who obviously put forth an awe-inspiring amount into this community (Pandora's) and to the survivors for their courage and bravery to survive this horror. Thank you Pandora's for bringing me to the next level on my healing journey.
>
> (By Kacy, Pandora's Project, slightly adapted)

### Rappel de méthode
En compréhension écrite, chaque réponse doit être une phrase complète (sujet + verbe conjugué), formulée avec tes propres mots autant que possible : reprends l'information du texte, mais reformule la structure au lieu de recopier des passages entiers. Localise d'abord le paragraphe qui contient l'information, puis réponds précisément à la question posée, sans ajouter d'éléments non demandés.

**1.** Plusieurs titres sont acceptables s'ils couvrent l'ensemble du texte, par exemple : *"A survivor's healing journey"* ou *"From abuse to hope"*. Un bon titre reprend les deux mouvements du récit : les abus subis pendant l'enfance et la reconstruction rendue possible par Pandora's.

**Questions**

6. 6. Name two significant things that Pandora's achieved in the life of Joan.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**6.** Deux réponses parmi les suivantes suffisent, en phrases complètes :
*Pandora's made Joan feel accepted, understood and supported for what she had gone through. It gave her hope, strength and stability to continue her healing journey. It also taught her that her reactions, such as flashbacks and body memories, were normal.*

### Piège à éviter
Ne recopie pas des phrases entières du texte : la consigne « use your own words » est évaluée. Une réponse recopiée mot pour mot, même exacte sur le fond, perd des points ; reformule au moins la structure de la phrase.

### Conseil
Construis chaque réponse en reprenant les termes de la question (*Joan was raped for the first time when...*) : le correcteur voit immédiatement que tu réponds à la bonne question, ta phrase est automatiquement complète, et tu évites les réponses télégraphiques sanctionnées.

incertitudes: Questions 1 et 5 : questions ouvertes, plusieurs formulations sont acceptables (exemples donnés dans le corrigé).
Le passage aborde le thème sensible des abus sexuels sur mineurs ; le corrigé traite les questions de façon factuelle, conformément au sujet officiel.
